title: Automated model for analysis of .IQ and .wav files along with signal parameter extraction
description:
• Background The raw data for analysis of signal collected off the air typically range from few Khz to Ghz bands. The analysis is being carried out manually to identify the signal parameters and the resultant data is then utilised for processing signals in the designated sensors. This data is often insufficient for fine grain analysis for parameter extraction such as modulation type, sampling rate, FEC, interleaving, etc. This creates a need for advanced data processing to extract the observation data.
• Description The terrestrial signals received from various sources includes data in HF, VHF and UHF bands. The raw data collected in the form of .wav or .IQ format to retain the characteristics of wave form. The analysis of signals is primarily dependent on the basic characteristics of data points selected during recording of these signals. Since the data point are recorded from different sensors and different locations, the parameters may vary. Therefore, the data available for analysis is often insufficient to clearly identify fine details such as sampling rate, modulation type, interleaving, FEC etc. This limitation reduces the accuracy and confidence of interpretation and data analysis that require detailed information. The data saved as .IQ and .wav have different parameters and therefore they store the raw information in different format. These files have to be processed in different ways for signal analysis to extract signal parameters. The problem can be addressed using advanced models such as GNU Radio, python, C++ to enhance the parameter extraction capability and more information rich inputs. The spectral relationship from training data containing both .IQ and .wav formats can be utilised for identifying signal parameters and carry out deeper analysis. The expected solution should be able to demodulate signals.
The GUI based model will have features to take .IQ or .wav file as input data and perform following tasks.
i.Identify signal parameters (Sampling frequency, Modulation, FEC, Interleaving). Additional features if feasible may be included.
ii.Demodulate signals (FSK, QAM PSK)
iii.Carry out de-interleaving (Block, Convolution, Diagonal, Pseudo Random).
iv.FEC (short-constrained convolution codes with Viterbi decoding, RS block codes, Concatenated codes, LDPC).
v.Bit stream correlation.
• Expected Solution The expected system should improve feature visibility of signals with the help of GUI, enable automated signal analysis to identify spectral features such as sampling frequency, constellation plot, water fall (time-frequency domain), demodulate signals, carry out de-interleaving and error correction. The output can then be used to carry out correlation of bit stream for identification of header and payload.
summary: Innovation (2/5): draws on standard software/hardware techniques applied to a miscellaneous problem, placing it in the incremental band. Feasibility (3/5): as a software build with moderate integration complexity, a full build is tight for 36 hours and will need scope-cutting. Impact (2/5): addresses a more targeted user group within Miscellaneous. Tech Depth (2/5): centers on model. Sustainability (3/5): will need a maintenance/upkeep plan post-hackathon. Scalability (2/5): currently scoped narrowly and would need rework to scale. Total 14/30 -> Red verdict.

detail.title: Automated Model for Analysis of .IQ and .wav Files with Signal Parameter Extraction

overview.in_plain_terms: Build a tool that automatically analyzes raw radio-frequency recordings (.wav or .IQ files) and extracts technical signal parameters, modulation type, sampling rate, error correction scheme, that currently require manual, expert analysis.
overview.why_it_matters: Manual signal parameter extraction is slow and inconsistent, and signals recorded from different sensors/locations vary, automating this speeds up downstream sensor processing significantly.
pain_points: Manual analysis of raw RF signal recordings is slow and expertise-dependent.
Recordings from different sensors/locations have varying characteristics.
Fine-grain parameter extraction (modulation type, sampling rate, FEC, interleaving) is genuinely hard and currently insufficiently automated.
overview.background: Raw signal data collected in HF/VHF/UHF bands as .wav or .IQ files requires manual analysis to extract parameters like modulation type and FEC, a slow, expertise-dependent process needing automation.
overview.whats_being_asked: An automated model analyzing .IQ and .wav signal files to extract signal parameters (modulation type, sampling rate, FEC, interleaving, and others).
expected_solution: Automated ingestion and processing of .IQ and .wav format signal files.
Sampling rate and related parameter estimation.

analysis.innovation_scope_note: Moderate as scored. Automatic modulation classification is an established signal-processing research area; genuine FEC/interleaving scheme identification from raw signals is a harder, less commonly solved sub-problem.
analysis.invention_effort_note: Moderate, achievable using established digital signal processing and ML-based modulation classification techniques, though genuine accuracy requires real RF/DSP domain expertise.

competitive_landscape.note: Requires genuine digital signal processing (DSP) and RF domain expertise, a narrow, technical field distinct from typical software hackathon skills.

innovation.note: Automatic modulation classification is established research; FEC/interleaving identification is a genuinely harder, less-solved extension.

invention.note: Achievable using established DSP/ML techniques for modulation classification; FEC identification is real additional technical depth.

technical_feasibility.tag: Comfortable for Modulation Classification, Tight for Full FEC/Interleaving Extraction
technical_feasibility.note: Modulation classification has strong existing research/tooling to build on; genuine FEC scheme identification from raw signals is a harder, less-standard problem.

impact_and_benefits.note: Genuine value for signal intelligence workflows, a narrow, technical audience.

architecture.note: A signal-ingestion and parameter-extraction pipeline, well-understood pattern for the modulation-classification component specifically.

overall_verdict.reasoning: Red, mainly due to genuine difficulty in achieving comprehensive parameter extraction (especially FEC/interleaving identification) at real accuracy within 36 hours. Scope to modulation classification and sampling-rate estimation, which have stronger existing technique support, while being honest that FEC/interleaving identification is a harder, partial-credit stretch goal.

evaluator_lens.biggest_strength: Modulation classification specifically has strong existing DSP and ML research/tooling to build on, giving a credible, achievable core.
evaluator_lens.biggest_risk: FEC and interleaving scheme identification from raw signal data alone is a genuinely hard, less-standardized problem, claiming comprehensive parameter extraction without being honest about this difficulty would overstate capability.
evaluator_lens.validate_before_commit: Scope your core deliverable to modulation classification and basic signal parameter estimation (sampling rate, bandwidth), which have real technique support, and treat FEC/interleaving identification as an honest stretch goal, not a guaranteed core feature.

idea_0_4: Source or construct sample .wav/.IQ files with known modulation types and parameters for testing.
Research established modulation classification techniques (both classical DSP feature-based and ML-based approaches).
Split: one person on signal ingestion/preprocessing, one on the classification/parameter-extraction model.
prototype_4_22: Start sampling-rate and basic signal parameter estimation.
integration_22_30: Test classification accuracy against your known-parameter test files.
Attempt basic FEC/interleaving pattern detection as a stretch goal, being honest about its limitations.
polish_30_36: Build a clear output showing extracted parameters against your known test file ground truth.
Rehearse presenting your modulation-classification accuracy honestly.
Prepare to discuss the FEC/interleaving identification challenge honestly if you attempted it.
build_plan.how_to_stand_out: Present your modulation-classification accuracy against real known-parameter test files, and be honest and specific about which parameters (modulation, sampling rate) you extract reliably versus which (FEC, interleaving) remain a harder, partial stretch goal, that honesty about differentiated difficulty is more credible than an overstated 'full parameter extraction' claim.

strengths: Modulation classification has strong existing technique support to build on.
Well-defined, checkable technical target with known test files.
weaknesses: FEC/interleaving identification is a genuinely harder, less-standardized problem than the PS's framing suggests.
Requires genuine DSP/RF domain expertise, a narrow, specialized skillset.

team_fit.ideal_ratio: DSP-heavy, this PS needs genuine signal-processing expertise, not just general ML skill.
team_fit.approach: Scope to modulation classification and basic parameter estimation as your reliable core, treat FEC/interleaving as a stretch goal.

ai_buildability_split.ai_can_build_fast: Standard ML classification model scaffolding for modulation type.
ai_buildability_split.needs_human_judgment: Correctly implementing DSP feature extraction and understanding real RF signal characteristics, that requires genuine signal-processing domain expertise.
ai_buildability_split.risk_of_leaning_on_ai_only: An AI-scaffolded classifier without real DSP domain understanding could produce unreliable modulation classification, especially for less common modulation types.

data_resource_availability.status: Signal datasets with labeled modulation types exist in some public research collections; specific FEC/interleaving-labeled data is much less commonly available.
data_resource_availability.backup_plan: Construct test signals with known modulation and basic parameters for reliable validation, be honest about limited data for the harder FEC/interleaving extraction goal.

judge_qna.question: How accurate is your modulation classification against real, known test signals?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Present your specific accuracy results against your known-parameter test set directly.
judge_qna.follow_up: How does accuracy change for less common or noisier modulation types?

judge_qna.question: How does your system extract FEC scheme and interleaving parameters specifically?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Be honest about the difficulty here, if this is a partial or stretch-goal capability, explain what you achieved and what a more complete solution would require.
judge_qna.follow_up: What's the theoretical approach for identifying FEC schemes from raw signal data without prior knowledge of the encoding?
